summary: Backend-only test of the encoding pipeline hang fix. 7/7 pytest pass (/app/backend/tests/test_iteration26_encoding_timeouts.py). E2E: a single tiny upload reaches ready/100% in about 7s with a 360p rendition and a preview_url. Back-to-back uploads (garbage + 2 valid) and a burst of 5 uploads (more than ffmpeg_concurrency=3) all reach a final status, so the queue does not deadlock. Unit tests: a hanging ffmpeg was simulated with a FIFO input that never sends data and asyncio.wait_for was capped to 3s. extract_preview_clip requests the 90s timeout, kills ffmpeg and returns False. transcode_to_resolution requests max(600, dur*20)=600, kills ffmpeg, removes the temp file and returns False. A semaphore wrapped around a hanging transcode is released and the next job succeeds. Startup cleanup verified: a doc in processing for 3h goes to failed/0 after a backend restart; a 30min-old doc and an old ready doc are left alone. Found 3 real issues (below): the main one is that a transcode that fails or times out is still marked READY with zero renditions, and probe, thumbnails and subtitle extraction still have NO timeouts, so they can still hang at 5%, 15% or 30%.

critical.issue: If every transcode_to_resolution returns False (ffmpeg error OR the new timeout), the loop finishes and still sets status='ready', progress=100 with renditions=[]. Reproduced: uploading 200KB of random bytes as .mp4 gives status=ready, progress=100, renditions=[], duration_sec=0, thumbnail_url=None, error=None. So with the new timeouts, a hung video becomes an unplayable 'ready' video instead of 'failed'.

None of these ffmpeg/ffprobe calls have a timeout (plain proc.communicate()/proc.wait()). Subtitle extraction runs AFTER progress=30 and the preview step, while the semaphore is held. A hang there freezes the video at 30% and blocks the semaphore, which is the exact symptom the user reported. With concurrency 2-3, all slots hang and new uploads sit at status=processing/progress=0 (waiting on the semaphore). That matches the screenshot (2 videos at 30%, 2 at 0%). probe hang = stuck at 5%, thumbnails hang = stuck at 15%.

minor.issue: When the 15s ffprobe wait_for times out, the ffprobe process `p` is never killed, so it leaks as an orphan process (confirmed: orphan ffprobe processes still alive after the test). Add p.kill() + await p.wait() in the except block.

Progress stays at 30% for the whole transcode (only updates after each rendition finishes). Settings use encode_profile='original' (preset=slow, crf 20), so long videos can legitimately sit at 30% for a long time and look 'stuck'. Consider adding an intermediate progress update, or warn the admin that slow profiles are slow.

Only resets processing docs older than 2h. Background tasks do not survive a restart, so ANY doc in processing at boot is orphaned. A video uploaded 30 min before a restart stays 'processing' forever (verified). The cleanup also doesn't set an `error` message. Consider resetting all processing docs at startup (single-worker) or re-queuing them, and set error='interrupted by restart'.
No `-nostdin` / stdin=DEVNULL on the ffmpeg calls. ffmpeg can block reading stdin in some supervisor or terminal setups. Cheap hardening.

It replaces the Semaphore object when the settings change. Jobs already waiting on the old semaphore keep the old limit, so the effective concurrency can temporarily exceed the setting (old + new). It does not deadlock.

action_items: In process_video: if `renditions` is empty after the loop, set status='failed' with error='all renditions failed / timed out' instead of ready/100.

Add asyncio.wait_for + proc.kill() timeouts to probe_video (~30s), every generate_thumbnails ffmpeg call (~30s each), and every ffmpeg call in extract_embedded_subtitles / _ffmpeg_extract_subtitle (~120s). Ideally move them all to one shared helper like _run_ffmpeg.
Kill the ffprobe duration-probe process when it times out in transcode_to_resolution.
Add -nostdin (or stdin=DEVNULL) to all ffmpeg subprocess calls.
Consider resetting all 'processing' docs at startup (not only those older than 2h) and set an error message.

rca of the issue: Reported: videos stuck at 30% and at 0%. Root cause: at progress=30 the pipeline runs the preview extraction (now has a timeout) and then embedded-subtitle extraction (NO timeout), followed by the transcode (now has a timeout, but progress is not updated during it). Any hang in the subtitle, probe or thumbnail ffmpeg calls holds a queue.semaphore slot forever. Once all slots are held, every new upload waits in `async with queue.semaphore` at status=processing and the default progress=0, which explains the 0% items. Mitigation: put timeouts on all remaining subprocesses, and mark videos with no renditions as failed.
